clue.text: Chaotic game (a draw) ends in general devastation?

indicators.note: chaotic means disordered, so the letters of these words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A drawn match descends into chaos and ends in widespread ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chaotic' rearranges GAME plus A DRAW; 'ends in' is a link to the definition, whose question mark admits the generalising stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Destruction caused by fighting, spread far and wide, is wartime harm on a general scale.

clue.text: West country person not going on stag-night

parts.note: Oman is a country in Arabia

explanation.surface: A West Country resident skips the stag night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West country' reads as England's South West; a stag night is a groom's pre-wedding party for men only.
explanation.definitionFit: Female people are excluded from a stag party, which is for male friends only.

clue.text: Never once managed to meet again

indicators.note: managed means handled or arranged, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A group never once succeeded in getting together again.
explanation.definitionFit: To assemble once more after adjourning is what a committee does when it resumes.

clue.text: A sign of possession that commonly isn't!

definitions.text: A sign of possession that commonly isn't!

parts.words: A sign of possession that commonly isn't!
parts.note: the punctuation mark showing ownership is often wrongly used in plurals, as in a grocer's sign for apples

explanation.surface: A mark of ownership that people often misuse.
explanation.definitionFit: This punctuation mark shows ownership, yet it is commonly misplaced where nothing is owned.

clue.text: Trees found in a dry environment, originally

indicators.note: environment says one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol, dry
firs are trees

explanation.surface: Trees growing in arid surroundings, at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: In the beginning is the sense of both, an adverbial phrase for initially.

clue.text: The dish and spoon, for example?

definitions.text: The dish and spoon, for example?

parts.words: The dish and spoon, for example?
parts.note: in the nursery rhyme Hey Diddle Diddle the dish ran away with the spoon, as a runaway couple would

explanation.surface: Kitchen items from a nursery rhyme as an illustration.
explanation.definitionFit: Runaway lovers who secretly flee to marry are what the rhyme's pair resemble.

clue.text: Force plus pressure equals muscular pain

parts.note: to force something in is to cram it
P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

explanation.surface: Like a physics equation: force added to pressure gives a muscle ache.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden painful contraction of a muscle is the standard meaning of this word.

clue.text: Detailed beliefs of some American Indians

indicators.note: detailed is read as de-tailed, losing its last letter

parts.note: a creed is a set of beliefs

explanation.surface: Elaborate religious convictions of certain Native American peoples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' looks like thorough, but is read as de-tailed: the tail is cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cree are a North American First Nations people, plural as a group.

clue.text: Quite enough try to go topless!

indicators.note: to go topless means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: to sample food is to try it

explanation.surface: Daring to bare all is quite enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Plenty, more than sufficient, is the usual sense of this adjective.

clue.text: It's like a sweet little French number

parts.note: petit is French for little
four is a number

explanation.surface: A dainty little French figure that resembles candy.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fancy cake served with coffee is a sweet morsel, akin to confectionery.

clue.text: Central comic role needed in kitchensink dramas?

indicators.note: central asks for the letters at the centre of the phrase comic role, dropping two from each end

explanation.surface: A comic part is essential to gritty working-class plays.
explanation.walkthrough: Kitchen-sink drama is a style of gritty realist British theatre; read literally, a kitchen needs a microwave, shortened to this word, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a microwave oven is called by this short form, an everyday appliance in any kitchen.

clue.text: River weed spotted on window-sill

parts.note: a river is something that flows, a flow-er in crossword jargon
pot is slang for cannabis, weed

explanation.surface: Someone spots a river plant growing on a window ledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River' is the old crossword trick of reading it as something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant container is a common sight on a window ledge, so the description identifies it.

clue.text: Injured runner? He withdraws from north-eastern ground

indicators.note: ground is the past tense of grind, so the letters are crushed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the pool of letters before the removal
taken as written, the two letters taken out of the pool

explanation.surface: An injured athlete pulls out of a race on a ground in the north-east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdraws from' removes H and E from NORTHEASTERN, and 'ground' rearranges what remains; 'ground' looks like a sports venue.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor who never begins a race is a no-hoper, and an injured runner would fail to begin.

clue.text: Let off steam if 27 goes topless

indicators.note: goes topless means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: the answer to 27 across, a competition

explanation.surface: Losing one's top is a way of releasing pent-up feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: To give expression to anger or frustration is the idiomatic sense of this verb.

clue.text: This may arouse you with its music

definitions.text: This may arouse you with its music

parts.words: This may arouse you with its music
parts.note: arouse means wake up, and a bedside device can wake you with a broadcast

explanation.surface: Something whose music stirs your emotions.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedside alarm combined with a wireless set wakes a sleeper with a broadcast.

clue.text: Try to find Indian, reported absent

indicators.note: reported signals that the word for the Indian is said aloud

parts.note: a Sikh is a follower of an Indian religion
someone absent is out

explanation.surface: An Indian man is said to be missing.
explanation.definitionFit: To search for and locate someone is this phrasal verb's ordinary meaning.

clue.text: Grasp a large whisky? Drunks might well

parts.note: to grasp an idea is to see it
a double is a large measure of spirits

explanation.surface: Drinkers who knock back large whiskies could well understand.
explanation.definitionFit: Blurred twin vision is the classic effect of too much alcohol.

clue.text: Learns nothing about Italian port

indicators.note: about means the letters are turned around into a new order

parts.note: nothing is zero, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone discovers nothing about an Italian harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: SALERN is the rearrangement of LEARNS.
explanation.definitionFit: This town on the Campania coast south of Naples is a seaport.

clue.text: Exotic blue rose gets left in sort of paint

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round
exotic means foreign and strange, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange blue rose is painted with a particular type of paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exotic' rearranges BLUE ROSE to RESOUBLE, and 'in' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Paint that can be dissolved again in water after drying is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Butler's place is nowhere special

indicators.note: special suggests the word is made different, rearranged

explanation.surface: A domestic butler's quarters are nowhere in particular.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Butler wrote a Victorian satirical novel named after an imaginary land whose name scrambles a word for 'no place'.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Butler's novel is set in an imaginary country, so it is the author's invented place.

clue.text: Labour's long expected (and welcome) result!

parts.note: labour here is childbirth, not the political party, and its awaited outcome is a baby

explanation.surface: The Labour Party's long-awaited election victory.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby just delivered is the welcome outcome after nine months of waiting and a labour.

clue.text: Canine companion could be Goofy

definitions.meaning: a canine tooth's neighbour at the front of the mouth, a cutting tooth
the Disney dog Goofy has prominent buck front teeth

explanation.surface: A dog's friend might be the Disney character Goofy.
explanation.definitionFit: Front cutting teeth sit beside the canines in the jaw, and Goofy's are famously prominent.

clue.text: Group member into booze, we're told

parts.note: into gives in

indicators.note: we're told means the drink's word is spoken, giving its sound

parts.note: cider is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A member of a group gets heavily into drinking, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone within an organisation, with inside knowledge, is a member of it.

clue.text: They symbolise the power of kings …. or heartless bankers!

definitions.text: They symbolise the power of kings

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: heartless means the middle of the word is removed, keeping only its two ends

explanation.surface: Royal regalia stand for monarchs' authority, or perhaps for callous financiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's regalia includes a jewelled globe carried as an emblem of sovereignty.

clue.text: Caliban has to live without routine

indicators.note: without means outside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: to live is to be
a rut is a dull routine

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's monster must live without a regular schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: Caliban is the savage servant in Shakespeare's The Tempest; 'without' in its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Caliban, the misshapen savage in The Tempest, is a beastly creature, an example.

clue.text: European car with jammed cylinders

parts.note: a Swiss person is European
Rolls is short for a Rolls-Royce car

explanation.surface: A European car whose engine cylinders have seized up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jammed' looks like seized, but means filled with jam: rolled sponge cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolled sponge cake spread with jam is a cylinder with jam inside.

clue.text: Jack who nicely complemented his wife

definitions.text: Jack who nicely complemented his wife

parts.words: Jack who nicely complemented his wife
parts.note: in the nursery rhyme Jack could eat no fat and his wife could eat no lean, so between them they cleared the plate

explanation.surface: A man who paid his wife a nice compliment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complemented' looks like 'complimented', but means completed: their diets fitted together.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme husband of a pair with opposite eating habits bears this surname.

clue.text: Aid provided by Lincoln and Taft, primarily

parts.note: Abe is the familiar name of President Abraham Lincoln

indicators.note: primarily means first, so only the initial letter of the president's name is taken

explanation.surface: Help came from two American presidents.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist, usually in wrongdoing, is the verb's sense, as in aid and abet.

clue.text: Aristocratic ichor?

parts.note: ichor is the fluid flowing in the veins of the Greek gods, so an aristocrat's version is the fabled colour of noble veins

explanation.surface: What runs in the veins of the nobility, like the gods' own fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble birth is described by the old idea that aristocrats have veins of a different colour.

clue.text: Ban from pub after semi-nude display

indicators.note: after places the pub's word following the half word
semi- means half, here the second half of the word

parts.note: a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: Someone is barred from the pub after stripping half naked.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclude someone formally is the standard sense, a synonym of prohibit.

clue.text: Competition in sport never rejected

indicators.note: rejected says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone never turned down a sporting contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A single contest within a sports meeting is the usual name for it.

clue.text: Slightest quarrel occurs in breeding-ground

indicators.note: occurs in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a bird's nest is where it breeds
a quarrel is a crossbow bolt, a kind of arrow

explanation.surface: A small row breaks out in a breeding area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarrel' looks like a row, but here is the archaic crossbow bolt.
explanation.definitionFit: The thinnest or smallest of margins is the superlative of this word meaning slim.
